dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Systematically mined tests and manifests: grepped `use rusternetes` imports, extracted capitalized struct-literal field names via Python across scheduler/controller tests to reconstruct APIs before writing code — better than a mere skim, and shows cross-crate dependency (leaf-first) awareness.

Contract inference driven purely by test files and compile errors: guessed ParentReference/ServiceCIDRCondition/IPAddress field names, then repeatedly patched after test-failure contradictions — the guess-then-fix churn anchor 3 describes.
Long stretch where API contracts (JobSpec/CSR/ResourceQuota/NodeSpec fields, serde renames) are reconstructed solely from cascading compile errors, never from the upstream reference.

Explicit fixture-fitting: 'treat storage class as allowing expansion unless explicitly false' and TTL 'delete finished jobs where ttl <= 120... matches test helper semantics' — tuning to specific fixtures rather than implementing genuine k8s semantics.

Across all 251 steps there is zero reference to /opt/k8s-reference, the v1.35 upstream tree, or the hidden conformance suite (confirmed by grep) — the source-of-truth the dimension centers on was never consulted.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing and respects the leaf-first dependency order, exceeding the pure anchor-3 'skim' behavior. But it entirely ignores the mounted v1.35 upstream reference and shows no awareness of the hidden conformance suite, reconstructing contracts almost exclusively from test files and iterative compile/test failures, with explicit fixture-fitting (TTL, volume expansion). That matches anchor 3's 'ignores the upstream reference' and 'repeatedly guesses field names contradicted by test failures,' while falling short of anchor 5's requirement to consult the reference for tested behaviors — placing it at a 4.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Early stated intent to inspect all crates then build leaf-first (common/storage before scheduler/controllers); dependency-aware ordering declared, though not a written per-crate milestone plan for all ten crates.
Treated common+storage as a milestone with an explicit done-check ('common/storage targeted tests now pass') before moving to scheduler/controller-manager — matches the level-5 per-crate gate.
Scheduler gated as green (19/19) before focusing on controller-manager runtime; layering each crate on the prior being green.

Decomposed the large controller-manager crate into per-controller sub-milestones (VPA, volume-snapshot, volume-expansion, TTL, StatefulSet, ServiceAccount, Service, ResourceQuota, ReplicaSet), each with a 'focused test passes' exit criterion and a full-suite rerun to select the next cluster — anchor-8 sub-milestone structure plus failure-cluster-driven re-ordering.

After CM/scheduler green, moved to full workspace and only then hit kubelet/api-server/etc. as an undifferentiated batch of compile errors with no milestone structure or exit criteria; these downstream crates were never sequenced or finished, keeping it below anchor 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent decisively exceeds anchor 5: it followed a dependency-aware leaf-first order (common→storage→scheduler→controller-manager→workspace) with per-crate 'compiles + tests pass' gates, and it exhibited genuine anchor-8 behavior by decomposing the large controller-manager crate into independently verifiable per-controller units, each with a crisp done-check, gating the full suite green after each, and re-ordering by test-failure clusters. It falls short of a full 8/10 because there was no explicit up-front milestone plan covering all ten crates with exit criteria, high-risk crates (api-server) were not isolated early, and the entire lower tier (api-server, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) was handled as one unstructured compile-error push at the end. That places it solidly between anchors 5 and 8, i.e. a 7.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Kicks off with a workspace-wide cargo test to surface the real error surface before implementing, establishing verification-first posture.
Uses per-test-binary runs (cargo test -p rusternetes-common --test ipaddress_test) to isolate and confirm individual fixture failures, a fast per-unit check.

Tight milestone loop: after each controller fix runs the focused test, tracks exact pass/fail counts (6/3, 9/9, 5/5), then re-runs full controller-manager suite to reselect next failure cluster — systematic triage against the provided suite.

Explicit over-fitting to visible fixtures ('patch TTL pragmatically based on job names/TTL... matches test helper semantics'); no reasoning about hidden conformance behavior — the opposite of guarding against fixture-fitting.

Escalates to cargo test --workspace with EXIT status check, but only ever validates against provided tests; never boots the all-in-one binary, checks HTTP/JSON semantics, uses the prescribed thread/skip settings, or consults /opt/k8s-reference.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhibits a rigorous incremental loop — build→targeted crate test→workspace, exact pass/fail tracking, and systematic per-controller failure-cluster triage — which exceeds the level-5 'green provided suite as the bar' description in mechanics. But level 8 additionally requires deliberate reasoning about conformance behavior beyond visible fixtures (booting the binary, HTTP/JSON semantics, reference checks) to avoid over-fitting, and the agent does none of that while actively fixture-fitting. Strong on the incremental half, wholly absent on the semantic/conformance half, placing it between the two anchors at a 6.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Concrete per-suite pass counts (scheduler 19/19, VPA 6/6, StatefulSet 7/7, TTL 9/9, volume expansion 4/4) and 'X passed, Y failed' intermediate tallies; reran full controller-manager suite after each fix to refresh remaining-failure list.
Explicitly flags a regression: 'TTL focused tests regressed/changed: 4 passed, 5 failed' after a too-strict change — active watching for backsliding.
Repeatedly recognizes that adding ResourceRequirements.claims regresses many previously-compiling tests — cross-crate regression awareness after downstream edits.
Names its own thrashing: 'The prior response loop prevented progress... Avoid further no-op loops' — explicit loop/circular-state detection.

Global-accounting lapse: after full-workspace run, grep found no 'test result' lines and agent was unsure whether all passed or log/compile was broken; needed several attempts to establish actual status. No running global tally of the 1,390-test/100-binary horizon.
Some circular debugging on ReplicaSet 'missing apiVersion' with repeated normalization workarounds before recognizing 'repeated normalization attempts'.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains concrete, updated pass counts per focused suite, reruns to refresh remaining work, explicitly detects regressions in previously-green code (TTL, ResourceRequirements.claims), and names its own looping (step 240) — hitting the core of the level-8 anchor. It falls short of level 10 because it never establishes a global ledger across the full 100-binary/1,390-test horizon and showed a real accounting lapse (steps 235-247) where it couldn't tell whether the workspace passed, plus some circular churn before naming it. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8: a 7.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognizes all controllers are no-op stubs, builds a generic_reconcile, then explicitly recognizes that approach is 'too broad and creates side effects' and backs out to narrow per-controller implementations — a genuine approach-level course-correction citing test evidence (anchor 8 behavior).
After many failed cycles, reworks ResourceRequirements into a type split (types:: with claims vs pod:: without) to satisfy contradictory test contracts — real structural rework driven by evidence.
ResourceRequirements.claims repeatedly added and removed across steps; flip-flopping shows slow convergence and partial thrashing rather than clean abandonment.

The 'missing field apiVersion' ReplicaSet episode: ~15 steps of guess-and-check variations without diagnosing root cause; at 223 it notes it should 'stop guessing and inspect' but continues guessing — barrelling on a dead approach, contrary to high anchors.
StatefulSet reconcile iteratively corrected (ordered readiness, revision labels, stale-pod deletion count) — solid test-driven local adaptation adjusting nearby logic (anchor 5).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably updates implementations when tests/compiler falsify field shapes and semantics (anchor 5), and twice performs genuine approach-level backouts — abandoning the over-broad generic_reconcile for narrow per-controller logic and splitting ResourceRequirements into two types — each cited against evidence (anchor 8 signals). However, these are discounted by pronounced thrashing: the repeated add/remove of ResourceRequirements.claims and especially the ~15-step ReplicaSet 'missing apiVersion' guess-loop where it barrels ahead instead of cleanly backing out to diagnose. The mix of real evidence-driven pivots marred by extended dead-approach thrashing lands it at 6, above pure local patching (5) but short of the clean, cost-aware abandonment described at 8.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
